title: Wilcoxon signed-rank test
biology: Microbiologists compare log bacterial density before and after a treatment in matched cultures.
design: Each independent culture contributes one difference; occasional large differences make ranks useful.
data_characteristics: One sample versus a location or paired differences
Symmetric differences for a location interpretation
question: Is the distribution of within-culture changes centered at zero?
null: The difference distribution is symmetric about zero.
options: exact = FALSE uses the large-sample approximation
conf.int = TRUE estimates a pseudomedian under the shift model
assumptions: Do not use ranks to repair mismatched pairs
parametric: Paired t test targets the mean difference
A model for heavy-tailed errors can preserve a mean/location target
nonparametric: Signed-rank uses ranks of absolute differences
If differences are asymmetric, use a sign test for direction/median

plot_args.note: Display changes on one horizontal scale

practice: Which alternative would you use if the distribution of paired differences were strongly asymmetric?
code_simulate:
set.seed(1105)
before <- rnorm(28, 6, .4)
after <- before + .28 + .28 * rt(28, df = 4)
d <- data.frame(culture = 1:28, before = before, after = after)
write.csv(d, file.path(output_dir, "data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
code_plot:
beeswarm(change, horizontal = TRUE, pch = 21, bg = "#73649A",
         col = "white", cex = 1.5, yaxt = "n", ylab = "",
         xlab = "After - before: log10 bacterial density (CFU/mL)")
abline(v = 0, lty = 2, col = "#B7663E", lwd = 2)
code_analysis:
change <- d$after - d$before
fit <- wilcox.test(d$after, d$before, paired = TRUE,
                   exact = FALSE, conf.int = TRUE)
generating_model: 28 baselines come from Normal(6, 0.4 SD). Paired changes equal 0.28 + 0.28 times a Student t variable with 4 degrees of freedom; after equals before plus change.
generating_truth: The symmetric difference distribution is centered at +0.28 log10 units; its zero-center null is false.
teaching_point: Signed-rank is useful for symmetric heavy-tailed differences; sign is the simpler alternative when symmetry is doubtful.
